children: Hackathon brings together 160 participants and 20 student teams to develop healthcare solutions and build pathways to commercialisation

The IIIT-Bangalore Innovation Centre, under the NAIN 2.0 programme, hosted MEDHA – Medical Device Hackathon 2026 in Mysuru on 18 September, bringing together students, faculty, healthcare professionals, innovators and mentors to identify clinical challenges and develop medical-device solutions. The programme was held at JSS College of Pharmacy in collaboration with JSS College of Pharmacy, JSS Academy of Higher Education and Research (JSS AHER), BETIC and IIT Bombay.

Around 160 participants attended the programme, with 20 student teams formed for the medical-device building hackathon. The initiative sought to connect real-world healthcare problems with technology development, intellectual property, company formation and investment readiness.

MEDHA 2026 aimed to familiarise students with medical-device innovation and entrepreneurship while providing exposure to clinical problems and multidisciplinary team formation. The programme also introduced participants to startup registration, patents, intellectual property protection, company formation and the investor perspective.

The event began with a welcome address by Dr T. M. Pramod Kumar, Principal, JSS College of Pharmacy, Mysuru, followed by an overview of MEDHA 2026 by Dr K. Bangarurajan. Dr Prashant M. Vishwanath, Dean (Research), JSS AHER, provided an overview of the institution's innovation ecosystem. Amandeep Srivatsava, Chief Innovative Officer, IIIT-Bangalore, was the chief guest.

A key component of the programme was the presentation of medical-device problem statements sourced from the healthcare ecosystem. Participants subsequently engaged in group discussions and formed multidisciplinary teams around the identified challenges. The programme included problem-statement presentations, team formation, announcement of teams and poster presentations.

Three knowledge sessions focused on company formation, intellectual property and patents, and investment. Abishek Bharadwaj A. B., Chairman, Mysore Chapter, Institute of Company Secretaries of India, discussed the advantages and challenges of company formation. Dr Chennamma, Associate Professor, Department of Master of Computer Applications, JSS Science and Technology University, addressed IPR filing and patents.

Sabareeshan C. K., Independent Director at BPL Ltd and Panasonic Appliances India Ltd, angel investor and startup mentor, spoke on the investor perspective and considerations for emerging ventures. The winning team will receive incubation support from the IIIT-Bangalore Innovation Centre, including assistance focused on company registration and taking its innovation beyond the project stage.

The initiative reflects NAIN 2.0's broader focus on strengthening innovation and entrepreneurship ecosystems across Karnataka's Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities by connecting clinical problem identification with solution development, IPR, company formation, investment readiness and commercialisation.
